_readme: PRE-EXISTING schema defects in baseline function bodies, recorded so the
guard fails on anything NEW while keeping these visible.
handle_job_completion has TWO defective INSERT sites (11944 and 11959).
An earlier report said 'eight remain live' (sites) but then listed seven
names (functions). Both numbers were right; the units were conflated.
TRIAGE ADDED: each entry now records whether the function is LIVE (attached
as a trigger, or called from app code) or DEAD (neither). A defect in dead
code has no runtime impact and repairing it can have side effects — see the
Fixing one means: repair in a forward migration, add a regression test,
then DELETE its entry here. Never delete an entry to make the guard quiet.
NEW CLASS FOUND 2026-08: writes to GENERATED ALWAYS columns (428C9).
transactions.net_amount_halalas is GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gross - fee) STORED,
so naming it in an INSERT column list is an error. Four baseline sites do.
The schema guard does NOT yet detect this class — see 'generated_column_writes'.

1482.liveness: DEAD-ish — no trigger; hire path runs through admin_dispatch_job / applications
1482.defect: INSERT INTO conversations (job_id, client_id, inspector_id) — no inspector_id column; kind and user_id are NOT NULL with no default
1482.canonical: conversations is BROKERED: conversations_kind_shape permits job_client_admin / job_inspector_admin (job_id NOT NULL) and help_support (job_id NULL). ensure_job_conversation(p_job_id, p_kind) is the canonical creator.
1482.impact: 42703 if called. Note the original intent — a DIRECT client<->inspector conversation — contradicts the current brokered privacy model, so this is not a pure column rename.
1482.status: NOT FIXED — needs the brokered-model decision, not a mechanical repair

7431.liveness: to confirm — organizations exist and are reachable in Admin UI, so another path evidently creates them
7431.defect: INSERT INTO organizations (name, kind, owner_id, is_active) omits slug, which is NOT NULL with UNIQUE constraint organizations_slug_key
7431.canonical: slug must be deterministic, collision-safe and unique
7431.status: NOT FIXED — safe to fix; needs a canonical slug generator

11099.liveness: DEAD — 0 triggers, 0 app callers. Its only consumers are the two dead settlement functions below.
11099.defect: INSERT INTO wallets (user_id, balance, frozen_balance, total_earned) — wallets has no frozen_balance
11099.impact: none at runtime; nothing calls it
11099.status: NOT FIXED — dead code; repairing it only matters if the settlement triggers are revived

11835.liveness: DEAD — trigger-shaped (IF NEW.status = 'cancelled') but NO TRIGGER IS ATTACHED, 0 app callers
11835.defect: INSERT INTO transactions (wallet_id, ...) — no wallet_id column; user_id (NOT NULL) unsupplied
11835.status: DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — see warning below
11835.warning: AUTOMATIC MONEY MOVEMENT. This function does `balance = balance + v_price` on the client wallet when a job flips to cancelled. Repairing it and attaching the trigger would create automatic refunds on cancellation. Requires an explicit business decision, not a correctness fix.

11944.liveness: DEAD — trigger-shaped (IF NEW.status = 'completed') but NO TRIGGER IS ATTACHED, 0 app callers
11944.defect: INSERT INTO transactions (wallet_id, net_amount, fee_amount, ...) — none of the three exist; user_id (NOT NULL) unsupplied. Canonical columns are gross_amount_halalas / platform_fee_halalas / net_amount_halalas.
11944.status: DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — see warning below
11944.warning: AUTOMATIC INSPECTOR SETTLEMENT. This credits the inspector wallet (balance + net_amount, total_earned + net_amount) and the platform (balance + platform_fee) the moment a job reaches 'completed'. Repairing it is precisely 'auto-transfer money when a job completes', which the payment freeze forbids. The fact that it is broken is currently the only thing preventing that behaviour.

11959.liveness: DEAD — second INSERT site in the same unattached function
11959.status: DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — same auto-settlement warning as 11944

16413.defect: INSERT INTO audit_events (event_kind, payload) — real columns are event_type / metadata; subject_table, subject_id and summary are NOT NULL and unsupplied. Its own duplicate-request guard reads the same phantom columns.
16413.impact: 42703 on every call. The defect is in the AUDIT write only — the function REQUESTS a release for admin action, it does not itself move money.
16413.status: NOT FIXED YET — safe to repair (audit-only, no money semantics change)

21231.defect: INSERT INTO transactions omits amount and type, both NOT NULL with no default in the baseline DDL
21231.impact: 23502 on every top-up credit, if amount/type are still NOT NULL
21231.status: NOT FIXED YET — verify the NOT NULL status against the live schema first; this records a buyer-initiated Stripe deposit, so repairing it automates nothing new
21231.fix_known: amount = p_amount_halalas / 100.0 (numeric(12,2) major units — convention confirmed from admin_fund_advance, which pairs `amount` major-unit with gross_amount_halalas minor-unit), type = 'deposit' (permitted by transactions_type_check)

generated_column_writes.liveness: LIVE — admin_fund_advance is called from apps/web/src/lib/actions/treasury.ts (the Early-Payout / Treasury admin surface)
generated_column_writes.defect: INSERT INTO transactions (... net_amount_halalas ...) — that column is GENERATED ALWAYS AS (gross_amount_halalas - platform_fee_halalas) STORED. Postgres rejects any explicit value with 428C9.
generated_column_writes.impact: Treasury early-payout funding fails at runtime. This is an ADMIN-INITIATED manual action, so repairing it automates nothing — it restores a manual control that is currently broken.
generated_column_writes.fix: remove net_amount_halalas from the INSERT column list at all four sites; it computes itself
generated_column_writes.status: NOT FIXED — found at the end of this pass; payment domain, needs its own tested slice
